item.content:encoded: This is incredibly minor (and I haven't finished reading yet) but as someone who frequently writes characters cutting in and speaking over each other, I would strongly recommend en dashes (–) over em dashes (—). The meatiness of the latter undercuts the swiftness of the dialogue transition, and the former is still distinct from normal hyphens' other uses.

item.content:encoded:
This tale is good, but there's a few things keeping it back from being excellent.

Some aspects I liked about this tale:

  • You hook us in with an interest concept that many people have asked: SCP-033 makes no sense, why is it an SCP file? This sets the reader up for the answer, which you inch closer towards from the start, while also getting us attached to the character. The tactics used here in lure the reader in are excellent, and are executed very well.
  • The answer works, and leaves the reader satisfied when finishing the tale. It also helps fills a gap, however small, in the Wiki's lore.
  • The characters are round and dynamic, and take us through a person's struggles as they live in the Foundation. It's interesting to watch these characters evolve while also jumping between the SCP-033 issue and the main character's issues.

Some aspects I did not like about this tale:

  • Way, way too much telling instead of showing. There are numerous parts of the article where you add unnecessary elaboration where there isn't any need for it. For example, "Ray thought about this. Colin's question was a fair one, but a difficult one to answer." Instead of telling us that it was a fair but difficult question, you could have portrayed that in the character's physical/mental response. Another example would be the back and forth after the start of the conversation between O5-11 and the main character.
  • The emotions that the characters feel throughout the article are generally angry or upset. This is not a bad thing, but the last section is contrasted with denial, shock, and general pacifism. The contrast and sudden changes in tone feel jarring to me, though there is a bit off padding when the tension decreases in the section before. I felt it could've been done a little better.

That being said, this tale is nonetheless good, and I would recommend it to others. Good luck in your future writing! ^-^

A hilarious and thought provoking Tale that is also a secret 001 proposal and uses the Archon class? 10/10.

Also on a meta level I'm glad you got this up given how much trouble you were having getting crit for it.

Edit: In IRC chat the author told me this is not meant to be a secret 001 proposal.

Still a really big fan of this. Last line is great, as is the whole conclusion to the story. I especially like the depiction of the discrimination felt by non-binary people without seeming overly preachy or ruining the flow of the article.

In conclusion, great work which is now becoming part of my headcanon!
